posts.text: Saudi Aramco Tower Damaged as Yemen’s Houthis Attack Riyadh — The Saudi authorities said no one was hurt after “falling shrapnel” hit the building in Riyadh’s financial district — one of the highest-profile areas targeted by the Houthis.

Why the Iran War Has Spurred Both Clean Energy and Fossil Fuels — The shock to global oil prices has caused a surge in demand for electric vehicles while propelling a race for immediate, secure power supplies.
US task force to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know — As fears of an escalation grow, Washington announces 'Task Force Iron Gate'.

An Iranian refugee's warning to American universities embracing foreign funding and radicalism — An Iranian refugee argues American universities must reject Qatar's billions and the campus radicalism that followed Hamas' Oct. 7 attack.

Trump ‘holds all the cards’ in war against Iran’s regime, White House says — Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei taunts America after midterms, but the White House says Trump holds all the cards on the Strait of Hormuz.

ROBERT L MAGINNIS: Iran War cost Republicans Congress. What will it cost America? — JD Vance blamed the Middle East conflict for Republican losses as Democrats flipped both houses of Congress after eight months of fighting Iran.
MAGA voters reveal who they want to see lead GOP in 2028 — MAGA voters at a Trump rally name JD Vance and Marco Rubio as early 2028 presidential election favorites after Democrats swept the midterms.

Why White Working-Class Voters Shifted Left in the Midterms — White voters without a college degree, a cornerstone of the Republican base in the Trump era, moved left this year. Some cited high prices, the war with Iran and more in their decisions.

Republicans Got Wiped Out. Now What? — Republicans suffered a historic midterm defeat, putting the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency and the future of the GOP in question. Daily Wire Managing Editor Dylan Houseman joins Tim Rice to examine what drove the Republican wipeout, from the Iran war and Trump's political baggage to candidate quality and voter frustration. They examine whether the results mark the beginning of the end of MAGA, why Democrats could face their own internal battles despite sweeping victories, and whether Republicans have an opportunity to rebuild before 2028.

More Than 50 Killed in Yemen in One of the Deadliest 24 Hours of the War — Strikes show the heavy toll since fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government reignited in August, with civilians paying a heavy price.

House GOP critics erupt at Stephen Miller as Trump elevates him after midterm massacre — House Republicans expressed shock and anger after Trump promoted Stephen Miller to chief of staff following the GOP's historic midterm losses.
